records.name: Eleone Dance Theatre
records.summary: A Philadelphia modern dance company that performs historical and new dance works that explore themes across generations and cultures, with a second company and an arts in education program.
records.what_you_do: See a performance, book the company for a show, or ask about the Second Company and Arts in Education programs.

schedule.text: No weekly classes are listed. Shows are posted one at a time on the events page.

cost.text: Show tickets are sold per performance, usually $20 to $30 in recent listings. No class fees or dues are listed.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for a public show listed on the events page and see the company perform.
first_step.basis: Public shows are listed with dates, times and a ticket link, so a first timer can see the company without joining anything. The page lists no classes or open rehearsals.
first_step.what_to_expect: Recent shows ran about an hour and a half to two hours. The February Black History program had a discussion after the show. Tickets were bought online ahead of time.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for the exact date, time and venue before you go, since venues change from show to show.
Buy tickets online ahead of time; school recital tickets are sold at the door.

records.notes: Summary and what_you_do carried over from tier 1 and checked against the deeper pages. The events page lists no upcoming shows and says 35 events were found in total, while the homepage lists a Black History show for February 2027 and a spring 2027 concert, and its banner says 30th Anniversary Season while the menu says 32nd, so parts of the site look out of date. The February 2026 show is named as Audenried with no street address. Second Company: no audition, schedule or cost is published; joining is at the Artistic Director's discretion and the page sends people to the contact page. Arts in Education offers a matinee, a lecture demonstration and a master class; no booking steps were found. Mailing address: P.O. Box 54340, Philadelphia, PA 19105. An RSS feed is linked in the footer; its URL was not captured.

records.name: Encore Chorale of Philadelphia
records.summary: A non-audition choir for older adults, run by the Encore Creativity program, that sings in four-part harmony with a professional conductor.
records.what_you_do: Sing at the Tuesday afternoon rehearsals and take part in the program's concerts, which are free and open to the public.

schedule.text: Tuesday afternoon rehearsals, 1 to 2:30 pm, during the fall and spring sessions. Rehearsals run about 90 minutes.

cost.text: Sessions are paid programs, and the amount is not on the pages checked. Tuition assistance is available, so ask the office.

access.notes: Venues are chosen with accessibility in mind, and singers may sit or stand during any rehearsal or performance.

first_step.how: Register for the Spring 2027 session when sign-up opens on November 12, 2026 at 12 pm; Fall 2026 registration is closed.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says singers of all skill levels are welcome with no audition, and anyone can attend the first rehearsal of a season to try singing before registering.
first_step.what_to_expect: Rehearsals run about 90 minutes and are led by a professional choral conductor, in four-part harmony. Singers may sit or stand during rehearsals and may sit during concerts. Fall concerts are usually in December, and the chorale's concerts are free and open to the public.
first_visit_tips: Come to the first rehearsal of the season to try singing; after the first week, singers must be registered.
Ask about tuition assistance before you register, since the amount is not posted.
Call 301-261-5747 on a weekday for questions. It is the Encore Creativity office in Washington, DC, open 9 am to 5 pm Eastern.

records.notes: Encore Creativity is based in Washington, DC, and runs this chorale in Philadelphia. The 301 number is its office line, listed on the register page under the Fall 2026 chorale; the group page itself has no phone. Fall 2026 registration is closed, and spring 2027 sign-up opens November 12, 2026 at 12 pm. The ensembles page lists other Encore groups in several states including Pennsylvania (Sentimental Journey Singers, Melody Makers, ROCKS, Broadway). They were not checked as separate records, so a Philadelphia lead may exist there. Rehearsal length is about 90 minutes per the ensembles page.

records.name: Esperanza Arts Center
records.summary: The Latino arts and culture center in North Philadelphia. It presents music, dance, theater, film and art from Latin America and the Caribbean, with family and community events.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a dance, music, film or family show, go to a gallery opening, or apply to the open call for artists. The center also runs workshops for neighborhood students and families, and the site gives no sign-up steps for them.

schedule.text: No weekly schedule. Shows, films and gallery events are posted on the calendar one at a time, including family events.

locations.label: Free parking lot and theater entrance

cost.text: Shows and films are ticketed, with prices on each event's ticket link. Season ticket packages are also sold.

access.notes: Free parking in the Esperanza lot at 406 West Bristol Street. Nearest SEPTA stop: the Route 47 bus at 5th and Bristol. Route 53 stops at Hunting Park and 5th, and Route 4 stops at 9th and Hunting Park.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to a family or dance show on the calendar through its ticket link.
first_step.basis: Events are public and sold through ticket links, and the site has a first time guests page. Workshops list only a contact email.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most people dress smart casual, and jeans are fine. The theater is kept cool, so bring a layer, and tickets are non-refundable. Events listed so far run about two hours.
first_visit_tips: Bring a layer, since the theater is kept at 70 to 74 degrees and can feel cool even in summer.
Check your ticket details at purchase, because tickets are non-refundable.
Park in the free lot at 406 West Bristol Street, or take the Route 47 bus to 5th and Bristol.
Read the House Rules page before you go, since it covers expected behavior.

records.notes: The getting-here page gives 406 West Bristol Street as the lot and entrance address and 4261 North 5th Street as the contact address; both are on the same corner. The calendar page returned not found, and the Plan Your Experience page only links onward. Tier 1 recorded a last sign of life of 2026-10 from events listed with no year; the only year on the homepage is the 2024 copyright, so that date was removed and status is probably_active (working site, no dated 2026 evidence found). Wheelchair seating, assistive listening and captioned or ASL performances were not found on the pages read. Hunting Park Business Association is named on the homepage as a dining partner; it is a business group and was not checked.

records.name: Park Friends Network (Fairmount Park Conservancy)
records.summary: A citywide network of neighborhood park groups, more than 140 of them, that clean up, plant, and garden in Philadelphia parks. The Conservancy and the city help run it, and joining a local group is the usual way in.
records.what_you_do: Join a park friends group near you for regular cleanups and planting, or sign up for a monthly city volunteer day or a Love Your Park service weekend.

schedule.text: Monthly city volunteer days on the second Saturday, at rotating parks. Neighborhood Park Friends groups have their own workdays through the year.

cost.text: No fee is listed on the pages checked for volunteer days.

first_step.how: Register on loveyourpark.org for a Love Your Park Fall Weekend service day, November 13 to 15, 2026.
first_step.basis: Anyone can register for a service day or join a city volunteer day, and the volunteer page says staff bring tools and gloves to the city days.
first_step.what_to_expect: The planting workdays listed run 9 am to noon. On city volunteer days staff bring tools, gloves and expertise, and some events provide tools and gloves. Volunteers are asked to bring their own water bottle.
first_visit_tips: Bring your own water bottle, since the loveyourpark site asks volunteers to bring one.
Check the event listing for tools and gloves, since some events provide them and others do not.
Call 215-988-9334 to ask which park friends group is nearest you and how to get on its list.

records.notes: This is an umbrella record. The network has more than 140 Park Friends groups, and individual groups are not listed here. Love Your Park Fall Weekend is November 13 to 15, 2026, and volunteer registration opened October 7, 2026. Spring Love Your Park Week dates are not published on the pages read; the spring recap is for 2025. The volunteer page gives the office at Ohio House, 4700 States Drive, Philadelphia, PA 19131. The email address is protected on the page and was not recorded. The site shows no minimum age for children and no waiver for regular workdays. The Natural Lands volunteer leadership application window is closed, with no date given, and it is not a separate record.

records.name: Fancy Brigade Association
records.summary: The association behind the Fancy Brigade competition, which is held indoors at the Convention Center on New Year's Day. It lists the brigades and posts ticket news.
records.what_you_do: Buy tickets to the indoor competition, or ask the association how to reach a brigade.

schedule.text: The indoor Fancy Brigade competition is held at the Pennsylvania Convention Center each New Year's Day.

cost.text: Tickets for the yearly competition are sold online through Ticketleap. The pages checked do not list prices.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for the January 1, 2027 competition through Ticketleap; the association says 2027 sales open October 15, 2026.
first_step.basis: Anyone can buy a ticket to the public competition. The pages do not explain how to join a brigade, and each brigade has its own website or Facebook page.
first_step.what_to_expect: The competition is indoors at the Pennsylvania Convention Center on New Year's Day. The association's pages do not describe seating, ticket prices, how long the show runs, or what a first visit is like, so ask before you buy.
first_visit_tips: Check Ticketleap for the current listing, since the association's site shows news about both the 2025 and the 2027 competitions.
Ask at 267-888-7348 or admin@fancybrigadeassociation.com about seating and how the show runs.
The association office is at 1100 S. 2nd Street, but the competition itself is at the Pennsylvania Convention Center.

records.notes: The association site is inconsistent. The top banner promotes 2025 tickets through Ticketleap, while news posts say 2027 competition tickets go on sale October 15, 2026 through Ticketleap, and one post said some tickets remained. Check the listing before buying. The member-brigades page names ten brigades: Avenuers N.Y.B., Clevemore Fancy Brigade, Downtowners Fancy Brigade, Golden Crown N.Y.B., Jokers N.Y.A., Satin Slipper N.Y.B., Saturnalian Fancy Brigade, Shooting Stars N.Y.B., South Philly Vikings N.Y.B., and Spartans N.Y.B. Each links only to its own website or Facebook page. They were not turned into records or leads in this pass: they are separate clubs with their own pages and need their own batch. The community service page does not explain how the public can help; it links to Caring for Friends, a Philadelphia volunteer listing source, which was not checked. The contact-us page returned not found.

records.name: Fidget
records.summary: Fidget Space is an arts space on North Mascher Street where artists rehearse and perform. It hosts evening shows of experimental music, dance and poetry, plus regular meetups for electronic music makers and free discussions.
records.what_you_do: Go to an evening show or a meetup, join a free Fidget Forum talk, rent the space for your own practice, or ask about artist residencies and the bartering program.

schedule.text: No fixed weekly schedule. Shows, talks and meetups are listed on the Upcoming page, mostly on evenings.

cost.text: Many shows ask for a suggested donation, usually $10 to $25, or a sliding scale. Some events are free, and the Fidget Forum talks are listed as free.

first_step.how: Come to a show or meetup on the Upcoming page; many ask for a suggested donation of $10 to $25.
first_step.basis: Public shows and meetups are listed with dates, times and prices on the Upcoming page, so a first timer has a clear way to come.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most listed events run two to four hours and start between 6 and 8 pm. Several are experimental or improvised music sets, and some are talks or club meetups. The Upcoming page gives each event's time and price.
first_visit_tips: Email info@thefidget.org if you want to confirm a date, time or price before you come.
Check the event listing first, since some events are free and others ask for a suggested donation.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the group runs book clubs and writing workshops. The site shows neither: the ongoing programs are the free Fidget Forum talks (since 2011, no set schedule) and the Process Project (improvised shows over a week), and the Writing page is a collection of works by the co-directors. The Upcoming page lists many 2026 events, the newest on October 3, 2026. Categories and interests are the closest tags, not exact matches: jam_sessions for improvised sets and variety_cabaret for multi-act nights. Food for Thought Fridays was a virtual series with its archive ending in 2022, so it is not treated as active. The Philadelphia Electronic Music Club is named as a meetup at Fidget; it is listed as a lead.

records.name: Fire Explorers
records.summary: A two year program for teens that teaches firefighting and EMS basics through Saturday training at the Fire Academy, and members who finish earn points toward civil service exams.
records.what_you_do: Train on alternate Saturdays at the Fire Academy in firefighting and EMS basics, and earn community service hours along the way.

schedule.text: Every other Saturday, 9 am to 5 pm, April through November, at the Fire Academy. From December to March, members may be asked to volunteer at some events.

cost.text: The program page does not mention a fee.

requirements.gear: Uniform, kept neat and polished at all times.

first_step.how: Fill out the online interest form linked from the Fire Explorers page on phila.gov.
first_step.basis: Teens aged 14 to 20 who are at least in 9th grade by April and who commit to two years fill out an interest form. The way in is clear, but a teen must apply before training.
first_step.what_to_expect: Explorers meet at the Fire Academy every other Saturday from 9 am to 5 pm, April through November. Training covers firefighting and EMS basics through classroom instruction and hands-on work with local and state agencies. Members also earn community service hours.
first_visit_tips: If you are under 18, a parent or guardian signs a consent form and attends an orientation.
To enroll, bring a copy of your birth certificate and your most recent report card.
Plan on the uniform: members must wear it neatly at all times.

records.notes: The program page names no year anywhere, and gives the start only as April with no day or year. Tier 1 recorded a last sign of life of 2024-04 from this page, but a full read finds no year on it, so that date was removed and status is probably_active (working city page, no dated evidence). The page names no street address for the Fire Academy, so only the program's own name is recorded. It gives no phone or email; the interest form link was not followed. Applicants over 18 without a diploma or GED must be enrolled in a program that leads to 12th grade completion. A web search snippet (not a fetched page) showed two different city email addresses for applications, so no email was recorded.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Electronic Music Club
leads_only.note: Named on Fidget's Upcoming page with meetups in May and June 2026. Its own website was not on that page, so it was not checked; it may be a Meetup group (leads only).

notes: Batch of 7 groups, 7 records, all publish. Searches used: 1 of 1. Fetches used: 35 of 60. Per-group fetches stayed at or under six. No rate limiting or bot checks seen. Not-found pages (404, not blocks): Esperanza calendar, Fidget visit page, Fancy contact-us page, and loveyourpark.org/park-friends. Corrections to tier 1: Fidget's summary, what_you_do, categories and interests were rewritten because the site shows live shows and meetups, not book clubs or writing workshops, and its status is now active (2026 events on its Upcoming page). Esperanza and Fire Explorers had last sign of life dates that a full read could not find on the page, so they were removed and set to probably_active. Esperanza's visitor entrance and free parking are at 406 West Bristol Street. Encore's phone (301 number, DC office line) was added from its register page. Dropped with reasons: the ten member brigades named on the Fancy Brigade site (separate clubs with their own pages, listed in that record's notes for a future batch); Caring for Friends (named on the Fancy community service page, not checked); Hunting Park Business Association (business group named on the Esperanza homepage, not checked); Encore's other ensembles on the same site (noted in that record).
